content:
Tiago Ferrão-Lindqvist
Data Engineering | Test Data Automation & Analytics

Setúbal, Portugal | tiago.ferraolindqvist@example.com | +351 555 010 311 | linkedin.com/in/tfl-example

PROFILE
Mechanical engineer with 12 years of experience in product design, testing and validation, now transitioning into data engineering. Builds Python tools to process test-rig data, apply specification-based quality checks and generate reports. Experience querying SQL Server test data, writing summaries to a staging table and building Power BI dashboards used by engineering teams. Currently completing an online data engineering course.

DATA ENGINEERING PROJECTS
Rig Data Processing and Reporting Tool | Corvane Automotive Components | 2021–Present
- Developed Python scripts to parse TDMS and CSV output from six test rigs, processing approximately 2 GB of data per week.
- Added checks that flag channels outside test specifications and generate standard report figures; reduced report preparation from about three days to half a day per test.
- Scheduled nightly runs on a lab PC using Windows Task Scheduler. The tool writes summary results to a staging table in the plant’s SQL Server database; IT created the table.
- Packaged the tool for internal use; four other test engineers now use it for their tests.
- Technologies: Python, pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib, npTDMS, SQL Server.

Test Results Dashboard | Corvane Automotive Components | 2023
- Built a Power BI dashboard using the staging table to show pass/fail trends and cycles to failure across product generations.
- Dashboard used by approximately 15 engineers in validation and design.
- Technologies: Power BI, SQL.

Bike-Sharing Trips API | Personal Learning Project | 2025
- Built a small Flask API over a public bike-sharing dataset loaded into SQLite, with three read-only endpoints; runs locally on a laptop.
- Followed a tutorial to run the project with Docker Compose.
- Technologies: Python, Flask, SQLite, Docker Compose, Git.

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
Test & Validation Engineer | Corvane Automotive Components, Setúbal | Mar 2019–Present
- Plan and run durability, vibration and climatic tests on seat-adjuster mechanisms across six servo-hydraulic and electric test rigs; prepare reports for OEM customers.
- Correlate rig results with FEA using ANSYS Mechanical and lead 8D root-cause analysis on field failures.
- Proposed a redesigned adjuster rail bracket that reduced warranty returns for the part by 40%.
- Query the plant’s SQL Server test-results database for trend analysis across three product generations.
- Maintain MATLAB/Simulink models of the adjuster drive used to select rig load profiles.
- Trained three apprentices in rig safety and test setup (2022–2024).

Mechanical Design Engineer | Halvik Pumps, Porto | Sep 2014–Feb 2019
- Designed centrifugal pump casings and impellers in SolidWorks, prepared production drawings with GD&T and owned DFMEA for two product lines.
- Performed structural FEA of casings in ANSYS; supported a material change from grey cast iron to ductile iron that reduced material cost by 12% for one casing family.
- Wrote a LabVIEW data-acquisition program for the pump performance test bench, reducing test setup time from about two hours to 30 minutes.
- Supported conversion of the performance test bench to a PLC-controlled setup, changing setpoints and timers in TIA Portal with an automation engineer.

EDUCATION
MSc Mechanical Engineering | Sado Valley Polytechnic | 2014
Thesis: Fatigue life prediction of welded brackets under variable-amplitude loading

PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT
Online Data Engineering Course | In progress; 6 of 9 modules completed

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Programming and data: Python (pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib, npTDMS), SQL, MATLAB/Simulink, Excel/VBA
Data and reporting: Power BI, Minitab, LabVIEW
Engineering: ANSYS Mechanical, SolidWorks, CATIA V5, design of experiments (DOE), GD&T, DFMEA, 8D problem solving
Personal project tools: Flask, SQLite, Docker Compose, Git

LANGUAGES
Portuguese (native) | English (fluent) | Spanish (good)

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is clear, professional, well structured, and substantially stronger than the original CV for a data-engineering transition. It uses measurable outcomes effectively: processing approximately 2 GB per week, reducing report preparation from three days to half a day, supporting four engineers, and serving a dashboard used by approximately 15 engineers. The project section makes the candidate's practical data work easy to find. The main content limitation is role seniority: the evidence demonstrates engineering automation and reporting rather than ownership of a production data platform. Some wording could also make the scope and limitations of the SQL, deployment, and cloud experience even clearer.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The document is ATS-friendly: standard headings, chronological experience, plain text formatting, readable bullets, and explicit technology names such as Python, SQL Server, pandas, NumPy, Power BI, Docker Compose, and Git. The separate Data Engineering Projects section improves keyword visibility. AI/ATS screening probability is moderate to low for this specific Senior Data Engineer – Data Platform role because the CV does not contain supported evidence for major screening terms including cloud platforms, BigQuery, Airflow, dbt, CI/CD, data modelling, production data platforms, query optimisation, or managed data warehouses. These terms should not be added because the candidate's material explicitly says they do not have that experience. The CV should instead emphasise its truthful equivalents: scheduled batch processing, data quality checks, staging-table integration, SQL Server test data, reusable internal tooling, and BI reporting.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV aligns well with Python-based data processing, SQL querying, data quality checks, reporting, reusable tooling, and collaboration with engineering and BI users. It also shows good professional English and Portuguese, both requested in the advertisement. The candidate's engineering background demonstrates ownership, problem solving, measurable impact, and domain expertise that could transfer to data engineering. However, the core senior-platform requirements are material gaps: the candidate has no production data platform or cloud data warehouse experience at scale, no Google Cloud or comparable cloud experience, no advanced SQL/query optimisation evidence on large datasets, and no strong data modelling or dimensional modelling experience. The candidate also lacks graph modelling experience. The personal Flask/Docker Compose project and ongoing course show learning initiative, but do not substitute for production cloud-platform experience. The document is therefore a credible transition CV, but a weak match for a senior platform role and a closer match for a junior or mid-level data-engineering position.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL / HIGH-VALUE CV CHANGES:
1. In the Profile section, make the transition level and strongest truthful platform-adjacent experience more explicit. Replace the final two sentences with wording such as: "Builds Python batch-processing tools for test-rig data, applies specification-based data quality checks, writes summaries to a SQL Server staging table, and delivers Power BI reporting used by engineering teams. Currently completing an online data engineering course." This keeps the relevant job-ad terms "data quality" and "batch processing" while avoiding any implication of cloud-platform or production-warehouse ownership.
2. In the Rig Data Processing and Reporting Tool project, change the first bullet to include the truthful operational context and scale in one ATS-readable sentence: "Built and operated a scheduled Python batch-processing tool on a lab PC, parsing TDMS and CSV output from six test rigs and approximately 2 GB of data per week." This more directly demonstrates the closest available evidence to the role's build-and-operate requirement without claiming a production data platform.
3. In the same project, revise the SQL bullet to clarify the actual database scope: "Writes summary results to an IT-managed staging table in the plant's SQL Server database; queries the test-results database for trend analysis." This prevents recruiters from interpreting the CV as evidence of schema ownership or database-platform design.
4. In the Test & Validation Engineer experience section, add the strongest collaboration and ownership evidence from the candidate information as a final bullet: "Trained three apprentices in rig safety and test setup from 2022 to 2024." This supports the company's ownership and collaborative working signals and is already supported by the candidate's material.
5. In the Technical Skills section, consider replacing the generic "SQL" label with "SQL / SQL Server (read-only test-data queries; staging-table reporting)". This is more precise and truthful, while still preserving the ATS keyword SQL. Do not describe SQL as advanced or add query optimisation.
6. In the Professional Development section, state the course status precisely as: "Online Data Engineering Course — 6 of 9 modules completed; in progress; no certificate yet." This is supported by the candidate notes and avoids any impression that the course is completed or certified.

MINOR ATS AND PRESENTATION ENHANCEMENTS:
7. In the Technologies line for the Rig Data Processing and Reporting Tool, add the supported operational keyword "Windows Task Scheduler" after SQL Server. This improves visibility for scheduling and batch-operation experience without implying Airflow or enterprise orchestration.
8. In the Technologies line for the Bike-Sharing Trips API, retain "Docker Compose" and "Git" but describe the project as "personal learning project" in the project heading or first bullet. The current wording is broadly accurate, and this clarification will prevent the project from being mistaken for production cloud deployment.
9. Keep the current standard section headings and plain-text formatting. Do not add unsupported terms such as Google Cloud, BigQuery, Cloud Run, GKE, Airflow, dbt, Spark, Kafka, CI/CD, dimensional modelling, graph modelling, or advanced SQL.

requirements.requirement: Experience designing, building and operating production data platforms or cloud data warehouses at scale
Advanced Python and SQL, including query optimisation on large datasets
Hands-on experience with Google Cloud or a comparable cloud (managed warehouse, serverless compute, containers)
Curiosity about new data architecture ideas and open-source practices
requirements.quote: Currently completing an online data engineering course; built a personal Flask API and followed a tutorial to run it with Docker Compose.
